name: Belgium
tagline: Three languages, six governments, the best beer in the world and a genuine talent for not explaining itself.
summary: Belgium is small, divided and quietly excellent at the things that matter daily: bread, beer, chips, painting and comics. The medieval cloth towns of Flanders — Bruges, Ghent, Antwerp — got rich early and kept the buildings. Brussels is the accidental capital of a continent and much better company than its reputation.

season.note: Spring and early autumn are best; Bruges in July is a queue. December brings serious Christmas markets and the beer suits the weather.

getting_around: Everything is within ninety minutes by train and the network is dense and cheap. Flemish cities are flat and cycle well. Brussels is bilingual on every sign, which confuses satnavs more than people.
food: Chips, twice fried, from a frituur, with a sauce you choose badly the first time
Trappist and lambic beer — Westvleteren, Orval, gueuze that tastes of cider and horse
Waterzooi and moules, and chocolate bought where it is made

festivals.name: Carnival of Binche, with the Gilles and the oranges

know: Language boundaries are legally fixed: French in Wallonia, Dutch in Flanders, and Brussels officially both.
Trappist beer is brewed by monks in six Belgian abbeys and sold to fund them, not for profit.
Sunday is genuinely closed outside the tourist centres.

regions.name: Flanders
regions.summary: The rich medieval north: cloth halls, belfries, Flemish primitives and a port that runs on diamonds.

cities.name: Bruges
cities.summary: A trading city frozen when its river silted up in the 1500s, which is why it looks like this.
highlights: The belfry's 366 steps and the carillon at the top
Michelangelo's Madonna, the only sculpture he sold abroad in his lifetime
The city at seven in the morning, which is a different city

experiences.name: Bruges before the coaches
experiences.summary: Day-trippers arrive from ten. Between six and nine the canals belong to you and the swans.

cities.name: Ghent
cities.summary: Bruges's rival, larger, younger and still a working student city rather than a museum of itself.
highlights: The Ghent Altarpiece, restored, in the cathedral it was painted for
Vegetarian Thursdays, a city policy since 2009

cities.name: Antwerp
cities.summary: Rubens's city and the world's diamond exchange, with a fashion school that reset the industry in the 1980s.
highlights: The station, which is a cathedral pretending to be a station
MoMu and the Antwerp Six's continuing influence

regions.name: Brussels & Wallonia
regions.summary: The capital of Europe, and the French-speaking south of forest, castle and old industry.

cities.name: Brussels
cities.summary: Art Nouveau streets, comic-strip walls, a gilded square, and the machinery of a continent in the eastern quarter.
highlights: The Grand-Place, best at night when it is lit and empty
Horta's houses, four of them UNESCO-listed
The comic strip route: fifty painted gables across the centre
Lambic breweries in Anderlecht, fermenting on wild yeast

experiences.name: A lambic brewery, spontaneously fermented
experiences.summary: Beer left open to the air of one valley, aged three years in barrel — the last place in the world doing this at scale.

cities.name: Dinant
cities.summary: A citadel on a cliff over the Meuse, a bulbous cathedral below, and the birthplace of the saxophone.
highlights: 408 steps or a cable car to the citadel
Kayaking the Lesse down to the river
Adolphe Sax's house, and saxophones on every bridge
